prompt.context: A public school system in a city has 130,000 students in total. The average score of the students in a state-wide exam is much lower than the scores of students from the rest of the state. The public school system has 13 grades: Elementary (KG to 6th grade), Junior High (7th and 8th grade), and High School (9th to 12th grade).
prompt.question: How do you improve the academic performance of the students in the city?

clarifying_info.q: How many students are there per grade?
clarifying_info.a: There are equal numbers of students in each grade (130,000 / 13 = 10,000 per grade).

clarifying_info.q: What does the school support system consist of?
clarifying_info.a: The support system comprises administration, a warehouse for storing textbooks, and special education (private coaching).

clarifying_info.q: What is the current on-time delivery rate for textbooks?
clarifying_info.a: Each student orders 2 books; 75% arrive on time. Inefficiency is caused 75% by warehousing issues and 25% by online order issues.

exhibits.title: Math Question — Additional On-Time Math Books for Junior High
exhibits.shows: A worked math problem describing textbook ordering for Junior High students, the split of inefficiency between warehousing and online orders, and proposed improvements under the McKinsey model.

framework: School factors: quality of teachers, teacher-to-student ratio, support systems (admin, warehousing, special education)
Student factors: time available to study, availability of study materials (textbooks), alignment of lesson plan and syllabus with the state exam
External factors: access to private coaching, parental assistance, distractions specific to the city environment (vs. rest of state)

questions.prompt: What are the key areas you would explore to identify the causes for the decline in academic performance?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure the problem into at least three buckets: school (teachers, support system), student (study time, materials, curriculum alignment), and external factors (private coaching, parental help, city-specific distractions). Strong candidates will propose data or diagnostics to distinguish which bucket is the root cause.

questions.prompt: The support system in school comprises administration, a warehouse for storing textbooks, and special education. How will you identify from these three areas where the problem could be?
questions.guidance: Candidate should suggest comparing metrics for each sub-area: administrative efficiency vs. benchmarks, textbook availability and on-time delivery rates, and utilization/effectiveness of the special education program. Probing whether any one area is an outlier helps prioritize.

questions.prompt: Each student orders 2 math books. There are equal numbers of students in each grade. Inefficiency is 75% due to warehousing and 25% due to online orders. Under McKinsey's proposed improvements, warehousing efficiency improves by 50% and online order efficiency improves by 80%. How many additional math books should Junior High school receive on time with the improved system?
questions.guidance: Candidate must correctly identify Junior High enrollment (2 grades × 10,000 = 20,000 students), total books ordered (40,000), split inefficiency into late deliveries, then apply the respective improvement percentages to each source.

math.setup: Total students = 130,000 across 13 grades → 10,000 per grade. Junior High = 2 grades = 20,000 students. Each orders 2 books → 40,000 books total. 75% arrive on time, so 25% are late = 10,000 books late. Of these: 75% warehousing = 7,500 late; 25% online = 2,500 late.
steps: Late books due to online orders = 25% × 10,000 = 2,500
Improvement from warehousing = 50% × 7,500 = 3,750 additional on-time books
Improvement from online orders = 80% × 2,500 = 2,000 additional on-time books
math.answer: 5,750 additional math books arrive on time after the improvements.

questions.prompt: (BONUS) We decided to move 6th grade from elementary to junior high. What are the implications? The current capacity utilization of elementary schools is 80%; they can host 6,000 students but only 4,800 are enrolled. There are 600 sixth-grade students. What is the new capacity utilization of elementary schools after moving 6th graders out?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute new enrollment after removing 600 sixth-graders, then divide by capacity. Should also discuss cost and operational implications (underutilized space, maintenance overhead, teacher redistribution).

math.setup: Current elementary enrollment = 4,800 students (out of 6,000 capacity = 80% utilization). 600 are 6th graders who move to junior high.
steps: Change in utilization = 80% − 70% = 10 percentage point decrease
math.answer: New capacity utilization is 70%, a 10 percentage point decline from 80%.

brainstorming.prompt: What external factors in the city (vs. the rest of the state) could be driving lower academic performance?

categories.name: Parental and Home Environment
ideas: Lower parental education levels limiting homework help
Both parents working longer hours leaving less supervision time
Language barriers in immigrant-heavy urban areas

categories.name: Private Coaching and Tutoring
ideas: Less access to or affordability of private tutoring

categories.name: City-Specific Distractions
ideas: More entertainment options (social media access, gaming centers)
Peer pressure or gang influence in urban neighborhoods
Longer commute times reducing study hours

categories.name: Socioeconomic Factors
ideas: Higher poverty rates limiting access to study materials

recommendation: Prioritize fixing textbook delivery by implementing the improved warehouse and online ordering system, which will provide 5,750 additional on-time books for Junior High alone
Address teacher quality and support systems through targeted training and resource allocation to the grades with the lowest exam scores
Pilot moving 6th grade to junior high at schools with excess junior-high capacity to improve resource utilization without new construction
risks: Junior high schools may lack capacity to absorb 6th graders without reducing teacher-to-student ratio
Underutilized elementary schools will still incur maintenance and administrative overhead
Improvements in textbook delivery alone may not be sufficient if curriculum misalignment or teacher quality is the primary driver
next_steps: Evaluate which junior high schools have capacity utilization below 80% before redistribution
Redistribute teachers proportionally to maintain or improve student-to-teacher ratios
Conduct a root-cause diagnostic comparing teacher effectiveness metrics and curriculum alignment across schools with the widest performance gaps
